_doc: Default settings of the shared controllers (JS src/flight/controllers, Python coldgas.controllers read this same file). A controller config {name, ...overrides} is merged over these. Changing a value changes pd trajectories: regenerate the parity goldens.

pd._doc: Heuristic autopilot on the four bottom nozzles. Attitude: alpha = att_kp * e - att_kd * w (e = body-up to world-up rotation, magnitude sin(tilt), growing to 2 when inverted), torque = I alpha, min-norm allocation with non-negativity shift. Vertical: track v_ref(h) = -sqrt(td_speed^2 + 2 brake_frac a_max (h - flare_height)+) (escape) or a height hold (hover tasks); collective only while cos(tilt) > tilt_cut.

mppi._doc: Sampling MPC (JS src/flight/controllers/mppi.js, Python coldgas/controllers/mppi.py, same algorithm, same noise stream, parity-tested). Every `replan` control steps: K = samples command sequences (piecewise constant over `knot` s, residuals on the pd pilot if base = 'pd', Gaussian noise `sigma` from mulberry32) are rolled out for `horizon` s on a rigid twin with integrator step plan_dt, and the nominal moves to their softmax-weighted mean (temperature relative to the cost spread). w_* / v_ok / curb_lookahead: planning cost (the task's own reward and success still score the episode).
mppi._doc_soft: Additions for the soft body (0 / 2 / 0 = the original cost): w_slip per step and w_td_slip at touchdown on sin^2 of the slip angle between the body heading and the horizontal velocity (counted above 2 m/s; the soft body scrapes its hull when it lands or rolls sideways, the twin's tyres do not); curb_steps probes of the kerb lookahead (at la*i/curb_steps) and curb_margin metres around each probe (the car's footprint, not just its COM); once a rollout has touched down, w_gnd_slip * sin^2(slip) + w_gnd_yaw * (body yaw rate)^2 per step (the kit car is 70 % rear-heavy: on the soft body it spins out ~1 s after landing, the twin barely does, so the closed loop has to pay for damping it).
mppi._doc_gate: bottom_gate (m, 0 = off): the residual on the four bottom nozzles is scaled by min(1, h / bottom_gate) (h = body-origin height above the street, 0 on the ground), in the rollouts and in the executed command, so the base pilot alone flies the last metres and the touchdown (base_pd: pd setting overrides of that pilot, e.g. a softer td_speed). On the soft body a 1-2 deg nose-up touchdown (harmless on the twin, so the planner does not care) lands the heavy rear first and pitches the rear floor into the street.
